data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise the Second Conditional for unreal, unlikely and hypothetical present or future situations.
learningPoints: Use if + Past Simple, would + base verb.
Use the Second Conditional for unreal or unlikely present and future situations.
Use were in formal or careful English with 'I/he/she/it' in hypothetical clauses.
Do not normally use would in the if-clause.
Use could or might in the result clause when appropriate.
Recognise hypothetical advice with 'If I were you...'.

sections.explain: Use IF + Past Simple, WOULD + base verb.

words.word: If I had more time, I would exercise more.
If I would have more time, I exercised more.
If I have more time, I would exercised more.

sections.summary: Using the Second Conditional for an unlikely future situation.
sections.explain: Use the form for something possible but unlikely or imagined.

words.word: If we won the lottery, we would travel around the world.
If we will win the lottery, we would travel around the world.
If we won the lottery, we will travelled around the world.

sections.explain: IF I WERE YOU is the standard form for hypothetical advice.

words.word: If I were you, I'd talk to the manager.
If I was you, I'd to talk to the manager.
If I would be you, I talked to the manager.

sections.explain: Normally use Past Simple, not WOULD, after IF.

words.word: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
If she would know the answer, she would tell us.
If she knew the answer, she would told us.

sections.explain: The Past Simple can be negative in the if-clause.

words.word: If I didn't have to work, I'd come with you.
If I wouldn't have to work, I'd come with you.
If I didn't had to work, I'd come with you.

sections.explain: COULD can express an imagined possibility or ability in the result clause.

words.word: If we had a car, we could drive there.
If we would have a car, we could drive there.
If we had a car, we could drove there.

sections.explain: MIGHT can express a less certain hypothetical result.

words.word: If he asked her, she might agree.
If he would ask her, she might agree.
If he asked her, she might agreed.

sections.summary: Using the Second Conditional for present impossibility.
sections.explain: The form can describe something unreal now.

words.word: If I lived nearer, I would visit more often.
If I live nearer, I would visit more often.
If I would live nearer, I visited more often.

sections.summary: Using a question with the Second Conditional.
sections.explain: Use WOULD + subject + base verb in the main question clause.

words.word: What would you do if you lost your phone?
What did you do if you would lose your phone?
What would you did if you lost your phone?

sections.explain: WERE is common in hypothetical clauses with BE, especially in careful English.

words.word: If he were more confident, he would speak in meetings.
If he would be more confident, he spoke in meetings.
If he were more confident, he would spoke in meetings.
